assumptions.condition: The schedule \(Y\) is fixed, and probability is taken only over \(A\sim\pi_{\exp}\).

For every \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), and \(r\in\mathcal R\), the potential outcome under a within-cluster assignment depends on that assignment only through own treatment \(z\) and the exact quota label \(r\), and equals \(Y_{ci}(z,r)\in\{0,1\}\).
The first stage assigns exactly \(m_r\) clusters to each \(r\in\mathcal R\), uniformly over all labeled partitions with these totals.

standard.name: two-stage complete randomization with fixed saturation-arm totals

assumptions.condition: Conditional on the first-stage labels, the treated set in cluster \(c\) is uniform over the \(k_{R_c}\)-subsets of \(\mathcal I\), independently across clusters.

standard.name: within-cluster complete randomization at assigned saturation

definitions.name: Cluster response type
definitions.construction: For each \(c\in\mathcal C\), set \(t_c=((N_{c,r}^{ab})_{a,b\in\{0,1\}})_{r\in\mathcal R}\in\mathcal T\), where \(N_{c,r}^{ab}=|\{i\in\mathcal I:(Y_{ci}(0,r),Y_{ci}(1,r))=(a,b)\}|\).

definitions.name: Exact cluster-mean kernel
definitions.construction: For \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(r\in\mathcal R\), and \(x\in\mathcal X_n\), define \[Q_{tr}(x)=\binom{n}{k_r}^{-1}\sum_{\substack{0\le j_{ab}\le N_r^{ab},\ \sum_{a,b}j_{ab}=k_r}}\mathbf 1\!\left\{x=\frac{N_r^{10}+N_r^{11}-j_{10}+j_{01}}{n}\right\}\prod_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}\binom{N_r^{ab}}{j_{ab}}.\]

definitions.name: Observed arm-outcome table
definitions.construction: Given \(A=(R,Z)\) and \(Y\), set \(X_c^{\mathrm{obs}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}Y_{ci}(Z_{ci},R_c)\) and \(H_{rx}^{\mathrm{obs}}=|\{c\in\mathcal C:R_c=r,\ X_c^{\mathrm{obs}}=x\}|\).

definitions.name: Compatible response-count fiber
definitions.construction: For an arm-outcome table \(H\), define \[\mathcal N(H)=\left\{N:\exists G\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal T\times\mathcal R\times\mathcal X_n},\ \sum_tG_{trx}=H_{rx},\ \sum_{r,x}G_{trx}=N_t,\ G_{trx}=0\ \text{whenever }Q_{tr}(x)=0\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Legal randomization tables
definitions.construction: For candidate counts \(N\), define \[\mathcal H(N)=\left\{h\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal T\times\mathcal R\times\mathcal X_n}:\sum_{r,x}h_{trx}=N_t,\ \sum_{t,x}h_{trx}=m_r,\ h_{trx}=0\ \text{if }Q_{tr}(x)=0\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Finite-population welfare weak order
definitions.construction: Define \(U_r(N)=C^{-1}\sum_tN_tu_{tr}\), \(\Delta_{rs}(N)=U_r(N)-U_s(N)\), and the complete weak order \(\mathcal O(N)\) by \(r\succeq_{\mathcal O(N)}s\) if and only if \(U_r(N)\ge U_s(N)\).

definitions.name: Pairwise centered max discrepancy
definitions.construction: For any arm-outcome table \(H\), set \(\widehat U_r(H)=m_r^{-1}\sum_xxH_{rx}\) and \[S_N(H)=\max_{r<s}\left|\{\widehat U_r(H)-\widehat U_s(H)\}-\Delta_{rs}(N)\right|.\]

definitions.name: Exact schedule-level randomization \(p\)-value
definitions.construction: For \(N\in\mathcal N(H)\), define \[p_N(H)=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(N)}\mathsf P_N(h)\mathbf 1\!\left\{S_N\!\left((\sum_t h_{trx})_{r,x}\right)\ge S_N(H)\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Worked three-policy closure test bed
definitions.construction: In \(\mathfrak E^\dagger\), compatibility is nonvacuous: for each of the six nonzero cells \((r,x)\), let \(t^{r,x}\) have \(N_r^{11}=4x\), \(N_r^{00}=4-4x\), \(N_s^{00}=4\) for \(s\ne r\), and every other response count zero. If \(N^\dagger\) places one cluster at each \(t^{r,x}\), then \(Q_{t^{r,x},r}(x)=1\) and \(N^\dagger\in\mathcal N(H^\dagger)\). Let \(\uparrow\) denote upward closure in the ordered-partition lattice and form \(\mathcal U_{12}=\uparrow\{\mathcal O:1\succ_{\mathcal O}2\}\), \(\mathcal U_{23}=\uparrow\{\mathcal O:2\succ_{\mathcal O}3\}\), and \(\mathcal U_{123}=\mathcal U_{12}\cap\mathcal U_{23}\). For any such intersection \(\mathcal U\) and an intersection-specific statistic \(T_{\mathcal U}\), the response-table oracle evaluates \[p_{\mathcal U}(H^\dagger)=\max_{\substack{N\in\mathcal N(H^\dagger)\colon\ \mathcal O(N)\in\mathcal U}}\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(N)}\mathsf P_N(h)\mathbf 1\!\left\{T_{\mathcal U}((\sum_t h_{trx})_{r,x})\ge T_{\mathcal U}(H^\dagger)\right\}.\] The construction handle is to choose the family \(T_{\mathcal U}\), apply closure to these lattice upper sets, and seek \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\alpha}(H^\dagger)\subsetneq\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^\dagger)\) while retaining uniform coverage and consonance.

definitions.name: Weak-order closure handle
definitions.construction: Use the exact compatible response-table maximization as an intersection-null oracle inside closed testing on upper sets of the ordered-partition lattice, impose consonance when mapping rejected intersections back to reported weak orders, and begin with the explicit three-policy instance \(\mathfrak E^\dagger\).

statements.statement: For every fixed candidate population with response counts \(N\), the response-type/arm/outcome table generated by \(A\sim\pi_{\exp}\) has support \(\mathcal H(N)\) and mass \(\mathsf P_N(h)\). In particular, \(\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(N)}\mathsf P_N(h)=1\).
statements.justification: This is the exact finite-population law that replaces an unidentified Gaussian covariance approximation.
statements.gap: Rigdon and Hudgens enumerate labeled assignments, while the available two-stage asymptotic theory records moments; neither states this multi-policy response-table quotient for order inversion.
statements.consumer: The table mass is the calibration engine for a reproducible exact-order module in the RCT2 saturation-design workflow.

statements.statement: For every realization of \(A\), the true count vector \(N^\star\) belongs to \(\mathcal N(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\).
statements.justification: Coverage requires the realized data never to delete the true deterministic schedule fiber.
statements.gap: The compatibility step is absent from generic rank inference and is more structured than scalar missing-outcome completion because first-stage totals and quota kernels must be respected jointly.
statements.consumer: This lemma permits analysts to coarsen to cluster means without sacrificing validity for the declared welfare target.

statements.statement: For every fixed candidate count vector \(N\) and every \(q\in[0,1]\), \[\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp},N}\{p_N(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\le q\}\le q.\] This inequality remains valid when the randomization distribution of \(S_N\) is discrete or degenerate.
statements.justification: Right-tail super-uniformity is the finite-sample step that handles lattice ties and zero-variance faces without regularity conditions.
statements.gap: Current saturation randomization tests obtain exactness only after sharpening individual-level nulls; this lemma instead conditions on a complete candidate schedule count and later takes a composite supremum.
statements.consumer: The result supplies exact calibration when the number of clusters is too small for the covariance-based procedures in existing saturation calculators.

statements.statement: Uniformly over every deterministic binary schedule \(Y\) satisfying the stated design and stratified-interference conditions, \[\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\ge 1-\alpha.\] The covered object is the complete weak order, so the assertion simultaneously covers all policy ranks, every partial tie pattern, and every zero-variance face. No pairwise allocation of \(\alpha\) and no cross-arm covariance estimator enters the construction. As an immediate reporting corollary, for each \(r\in\mathcal R\), take the union of the integer positions occupied by \(r\) over the retained weak orders, letting a tied block contribute every position that it spans. With the same probability, these rank sets simultaneously contain every policy's true tied-rank interval.
statements.justification: This is the missing finite-sample simultaneous coverage theorem for exact-quota policy rankings.
statements.gap: Mogstad et al. require a valid simultaneous difference region, Rigdon and Hudgens cover scalar effects, and Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong reserve finite-sample validity for stronger individual-level restrictions rather than the weak average welfare order.
statements.consumer: RCT2 and the Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--\u00d6zler design calculator can report which complete and tied policy orderings remain compatible with the realized experiment at level \(1-\alpha\).

statements.statement: The confidence set \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is exactly equal to the result of labeled sharp-schedule inversion based on the coarsened cluster means and discrepancy \(S_N\). Cross-policy alignment of individual response labels does not change compatibility, welfare, the discrepancy, or any table probability. For a finite-instance reference algorithm, set \(d=K(n+1)|\mathcal T|\), \(B_N=\binom{C+|\mathcal T|-1}{|\mathcal T|-1}\), and \(B_H=\binom{C+d-1}{d-1}\). Precomputing the kernels and streaming over all candidate counts and all nonnegative \(d\)-cell response tables gives the explicit upper bound \(O(K|\mathcal T|n^4+(d+K^2)B_NB_H)\) exact-rational arithmetic operations, before bit-complexity costs; legality and compatibility constraints only reduce this enumeration. Here \(|\mathcal T|=\binom{n+3}{3}^{K}\), so the bound is intentionally exponential. By contrast, direct labeled-schedule enumeration ranges over as many as \(2^{2KnC}\) binary potential-outcome schedules and, for each schedule, at most \(K^C2^{nC}\) assignment points. The response-table bound is a finite quotient reference, not a polynomial-time guarantee.
statements.justification: Without this quotient the exact confidence set is only a conceptual union over exponentially many labeled missing potential outcomes.
statements.gap: Rigdon and Hudgens' scalar algorithm samples labeled sharp schedules, and Bazylik et al.'s exact rank computation uses a multinomial binomial-conditioning identity unavailable under two-stage exact quotas.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives software authors a finite, auditable reference algorithm and a ground truth against which pruning or branch-and-bound implementations can be checked.

statements.statement: Using the weak-order closure handle, can one construct a consonant exact procedure \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}^{\mathrm{cl}}_{\alpha}\) that has the same uniform simultaneous coverage as \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}\), is contained in it for every observed table, is strictly contained for at least one nondegenerate compatible table, and remains computable solely through finitely many compatible response-table maximizations?
statements.justification: Exact schedule supremization can be conservative; a logically coherent strict refinement is the central open power problem.
statements.gap: Mogstad et al. use stepwise directional testing, but no checked result supplies consonant closure for composite exact-quota schedule fibers with fixed arm totals.
statements.consumer: A successful refinement would shorten simultaneous policy-rank reports without weakening the exact design guarantee used by small-cluster saturation trials.

sampling_model.design: Two-stage complete randomization: exact first-stage totals \(m_r\) and uniform within-cluster \(k_r\)-subsets.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(C\) labeled clusters, each with \(n\) labeled units and deterministic binary potential outcomes.
sampling_model.treatment: Policy \(r\) assigns the exact interior quota \(k_r\); own treatment is binary and stratified interference indexes outcomes by \((z,r)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every quota is interior, \(1\le k_r\le n-1\), and every first-stage arm total is positive, \(m_r\ge1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function or covariance is estimated. Composite-null uncertainty is handled by exact maximization over \(\mathcal N(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.3 maps simultaneous pairwise-difference coverage into simultaneous confidence sets for all ranks.
Section 4.1 inverts maximized sharp-schedule randomization tests to cover one scalar binary interference effect.
Corollary 2.1 gives finite-sample rank coverage from conditional binomial pair tests under multinomial sampling.
Proposition 4.1 validates an artificial conditional experiment by partitioning the original assignment support.
Theorems 3.1 and 5.1 establish finite-sample tests for individual-level saturation restrictions.
Theorems 2--5 derive joint design covariance, conservative variance estimation, and asymptotic tests for saturation effects.
Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 characterize sharp finite-population variance bounds and their asymptotically sharp estimators.
Theorem 1 supplies finite-sample upper bounds on empirical-success saturation-ranking regret.

tldr: Exact-quota experiments report empirical rankings of saturation policies, but neither asymptotic rank intervals nor scalar exact interference intervals provide a finite-sample confidence set for the entire welfare weak order. The project inverts a single max-discrepancy randomization test over every binary stratified-interference schedule compatible with the observed cluster means. A response-type quotient and an exact factorial table law turn that apparently labeled-schedule construction into a finite integer-table algorithm. The resulting random set covers the full weak order with probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over deterministic schedules, including partial ties and zero-variance faces, without estimating unidentified cross-arm covariance products or applying a pairwise Bonferroni correction.

project_justification.gap: Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm construct simultaneous rank sets from valid simultaneous confidence regions for pairwise differences, while Rigdon and Hudgens invert exact tests for scalar interference effects. Bazylik, Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm obtain finite-sample rank sets only by exploiting a multinomial conditional law. None supplies an exact randomization-valid confidence set for the joint weak order of quota-policy welfares under fixed first-stage arm totals and within-cluster exact quotas.
project_justification.niche: Binary stratified interference and fixed cluster size create a finite response alphabet. This makes the otherwise infeasible union over sharp potential-outcome schedules exactly reducible to compatible response-type counts and exact arm-outcome tables, even though cross-arm potential-outcome products are unidentified.
project_justification.fill: The core defines a max-discrepancy schedule-level randomization \(p\)-value, maximizes it over each weak-order fiber, and retains precisely the weak orders not rejected. The exact table law proves finite-sample simultaneous coverage, and the compression theorem supplies a finite algorithm whose operations are integer feasibility checks and rational table summation.

related_work: Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm motivate simultaneous rank uncertainty and prove that a valid simultaneous region for pairwise differences transfers to rank coverage; their published construction is asymptotic in the generic setting and informs the reporting map here. Rigdon and Hudgens provide the closest inferential move: invert exact randomization tests over compatible binary potential-outcome schedules for scalar direct and spillover effects; their construction informs the schedule-supremum step but does not address a joint policy weak order. Bazylik, Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm obtain finite-sample rank confidence sets for multinomial counts by conditioning a pair to a binomial experiment; that nuisance-elimination identity is unavailable for heterogeneous exact-quota response kernels. Athey, Eckles, and Imbens show how artificial conditional experiments can sharpen certain interference nulls; weak average welfare ordering does not impute focal outcomes, so the present construction instead ranges over complete compatible schedules. Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong give finite-sample saturation tests for individual-level partially sharp, bounded, and monotone restrictions and asymptotic tests for weak averages; the target here is the finite-population weak order of policy-average welfare. Jiang, Imai, and Malani derive joint asymptotic covariance and power calculations for two-stage designs, while Aronow, Green, and Lee sharply bound unidentified randomization variance through extremal coupling; neither object determines an exact composite joint tail. Han, Owusu, and Shin analyze empirical saturation-ranking regret and a surrogate design criterion, not confidence coverage. These papers inform the proposal; the core does not promise to tighten any of their theorem-level bounds.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite reference algorithm has the explicit response-table arithmetic bound \(O(K|\mathcal T|n^4+(d+K^2)B_NB_H)\), where \(d=K(n+1)|\mathcal T|\), \(B_N=\binom{C+|\mathcal T|-1}{|\mathcal T|-1}\), and \(B_H=\binom{C+d-1}{d-1}\); bit complexity is additional. This is exponential and is distinct from direct labeled enumeration of up to \(2^{2KnC}\) potential-outcome schedules times at most \(K^C2^{nC}\) assignment points. The table quotient is therefore an auditable finite reference, not a claimed polynomial-time implementation. The proposed coverage theorem does not require the fixed positive welfare gaps used by the ranking-exponent program; this is essential for ties, but it also means the reported set can be wide. The exact \(C=8\), \(m_2=6\) endpoint-envelope kill test from the presolve draft was independently reproduced: all \(526\) feasible welfare-count vectors were enumerated, and the maximum endpoint-hit probability was \(37/1306368\), attained at counts \((1,0,0,0,6,0,0,0,1)\). That check validates the inherited exact-table arithmetic but is not evidence for the coverage theorem.
honest_scope: The settled target for this proposal is coverage and exact finite compression, not shortness optimality, polynomial complexity, or a released calculator. The consonant strict refinement is explicitly open. The worked \(K=3\) response table fixes a nonempty compatible fiber, concrete lattice upper sets, the exact intersection-null oracle, and the strict-containment target; it does not assert that statistics attaining that target exist. When \(K=2\), the coverage theorem reduces to the familiar inversion of an exact randomization test for the sign of one finite-population welfare contrast; this is the required standard special-case reduction. Partial ties are represented as tied blocks of a complete weak order rather than broken by an arbitrary empirical tie rule.

seed_details.title: Exact response-table confidence set for the full welfare weak order
seed_details.anchor: RigdonHudgens2015, Sections 1, 4.1, and 6; MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024, Theorem 3.3 and Section 5
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a finite-sample exact simultaneous confidence set for the weak order of all exact-quota finite-population policy welfares.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar effect-value inversion by a supremum over compatible schedule fibers indexed by ordered partitions, and quotient the randomization orbit by response-type/arm/outcome tables before calibrating one global max-discrepancy statistic.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched pair \(\{\text{exact randomization inversion}\}\times\{\text{saturation-policy weak order}\}\) returned scalar exact intervals, asymptotic rank sets, multinomial exact ranks, and a unit-level monotonicity test, but no exact weak-order confidence set for finite-population policy welfare.
seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee will call this an immediate vectorization of Rigdon and Hudgens followed by the rank projection of Mogstad et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: The coverage logic is deliberately inherited, but the new kernel is the exact quotient: compatibility, composite-null maximization, and the full randomization distribution are all represented by one finite response-table fiber with fixed arm totals, so no labeled schedule enumeration, covariance plug-in, or pairwise multiplicity split is required.

seed_details.title: Consonant closed testing on the weak-order lattice
seed_details.opportunity: Replace a rectangular rank projection by exact closure over logically nested weak-order nulls in the quota experiment.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace stepwise directional-error control for pairwise differences by closure over upper sets of the ordered-partition lattice, with each intersection null calibrated through the compatible response-table oracle.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched pair \(\{\text{closed testing}\}\times\{\text{exact saturation weak orders}\}\) yielded generic rank procedures and exact multinomial pair tests, but no response-table closure theorem.
seed_details.red_team: The construction may be only a computationally explosive restatement of the closure principle.
seed_details.rebuttal: A nontrivial result would have to prove consonance, exact strong directional control, and a strict data-dependent containment relative to the single-step order set using the same table oracle; these properties do not follow from closure alone.

seed_details.title: Exact confidence set for the identities of the best quota policies
seed_details.opportunity: Invert the compatible-table randomization law directly for the set of welfare maximizers, allowing ties.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the asymptotic multiple-testing input for the \(\tau\)-best set by a composite exact test over schedules whose argmax set satisfies the candidate null.
seed_details.destination_search: Search found inference on winners and generic best-set procedures, but no exact-quota finite-population maximizer set under stratified interference.
seed_details.red_team: This is a strict subproblem of the full weak-order confidence set.
seed_details.rebuttal: The direct inversion may be materially shorter than projecting a full order set, but it offers less scientific output and is therefore retained only as a fallback.

seed_details.title: Sharp covariance-robust Wald weak-order set
seed_details.opportunity: Optimize simultaneous Gaussian critical values over compatible cross-arm covariance couplings.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Lift the two-margin Hoeffding coupling bound to the joint covariance image of all quota-specific cluster means before calibrating a rank cone.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination contains sharp variance bounds and asymptotic saturation inference, but not a finite-sample weak-order coverage theorem.
seed_details.red_team: This merely repackages a sharp covariance set and still cannot yield exact small-sample coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated finite-sample target because a covariance image alone controls neither discrete joint tails nor zero-variance faces.

seed_details.title: Conditional artificial experiment for weak welfare-order nulls
seed_details.opportunity: Choose focal clusters so that a nonsharp average-welfare order becomes sharp under conditional quota relabeling.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct a partition of the two-stage assignment space on which every pairwise weak welfare inequality imputes the focal cluster outcomes.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest saturation construction gives finite-sample validity for individual-level partially sharp or bounded nulls, but treats weak average nulls only asymptotically.
seed_details.red_team: An average welfare inequality does not impute missing focal outcomes, so the desired artificial experiment need not exist without strengthening the null.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds: strengthening to an individual-level null changes the estimand and would violate the requested weak-order target.

seed_details.title: Bonferroni assembly of scalar exact welfare-difference intervals
seed_details.opportunity: Apply scalar schedule inversion to every quota pair and project the simultaneous intervals to ranks.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Repeat the scalar exact inversion for each welfare contrast and allocate \(\alpha\) across pairs.
seed_details.destination_search: Both ingredients are published and their composition requires no new probability argument.
seed_details.red_team: This is immediate from the two anchor papers.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; the seed is discarded in favor of one global schedule test and exact table compression.

seed_details.title: Nuisance-free conditional pair tests for quota welfares
seed_details.opportunity: Find a conditional statistic that removes all schedule nuisance parameters from each pairwise quota-welfare comparison.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition on an exact sufficient margin for the response-table pair and seek a monotone-likelihood-ratio family indexed only by the welfare difference.
seed_details.destination_search: The multinomial rank problem has such a binomial conditional law, but exact-quota response tables retain type-specific kernel nuisance after natural margins are fixed.
seed_details.red_team: No low-dimensional sufficient margin exists for the heterogeneous response-kernel family.
seed_details.rebuttal: The search obstruction is persuasive and no defensible conditional reduction was found, so the seed is not padded into the core.

seed_details.title: Exact zero-error and partial-tie face classification
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize which compatible schedule fibers force a policy relation under every assignment.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace endpoint bounds for one scalar effect by an if-and-only-if separation condition between every compatible response-table support and each adverse order face.
seed_details.destination_search: No published exact saturation-order face classification was found.
seed_details.red_team: The classification is a direct emptiness check once the response-table fiber has been defined.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection substantially holds unless a closed-form combinatorial characterization is found; finite enumeration alone is not a separate theorem contribution.

seed_details.title: Inference-aware exact-quota allocation
seed_details.opportunity: Choose exact first-stage totals to minimize the worst-case expected cardinality of an exact weak-order confidence set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace variance-based sample-size optimization by a discrete minimax criterion computed from the compatible order-set inversion.
seed_details.destination_search: Existing saturation calculators optimize power or variance, and ranking-design work optimizes regret bounds, not exact order-set size.
seed_details.red_team: The criterion depends on unobserved schedules and nests an intractable confidence-set calculation inside design optimization.
seed_details.rebuttal: A saddle certificate could overcome the objection, but no tractable reduction survived the initial scan; combining design choice and exact inversion is too broad for this version.

seed_details.title: Randomized boundary calibration for exact nominal order coverage
seed_details.opportunity: Randomize on discrete \(p\)-value boundaries so the true weak order has coverage exactly \(1-\alpha\) when its schedule fiber is nondegenerate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Attach an auxiliary uniform variable to the schedule-specific tail probability and coordinate boundary randomization across order fibers.
seed_details.destination_search: Randomized exact tests are standard, while no consumer need for randomized reporting of policy orders was found.
seed_details.red_team: Exact-size boundary randomization is textbook and operationally unattractive.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; conservative nonrandomized coverage is the scientifically preferable target.

literature_map.settled: A simultaneous confidence region for all pairwise differences yields simultaneous rank coverage. Under multinomial sampling, conditional binomial tests and Holm adjustment give finite-sample rank sets.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: Neither result supplies the randomization law or compatible-schedule inversion for exact-quota saturation welfares.
literature_map.checked_locations: Mogstad et al., Introduction, Theorem 3.3, Remark 3.8, and Conclusion; Bazylik et al., Introduction, Theorems 2.1--2.2, Algorithm 2.1, and Corollary 2.1.

literature_map.settled: For binary stratified-interference outcomes, maximizing sharp-null randomization \(p\)-values over schedules mapping to a scalar causal-effect value gives an exact confidence set.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: The paper does not form a joint weak-order set across three or more quota policies or derive the response-type table quotient used here.

literature_map.thread: Artificial experiments and current saturation randomization tests
literature_map.settled: Artificial conditioning yields exact tests when a nonsharp interference null becomes sharp on focal units. In randomized saturation designs, individual-level partially sharp, bounded, and monotone spillover nulls admit finite-sample tests, whereas weak average nulls receive asymptotic calibration.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: A finite-population weak order concerns average policy welfares and does not sharpen under the available focal-unit conditions; the schedule-supremum route remains distinct.
literature_map.checked_locations: Athey et al., Introduction, Section 4, Proposition 4.1, and Conclusion; Liu et al., Introduction, Theorems 3.1 and 5.1, and Conclusion.

literature_map.thread: Two-stage covariance, power, and ranking regret
literature_map.settled: Joint design covariance supports asymptotic Wald tests and power calculations; sharp coupling bounds address unidentified finite-population variance; empirical-success ranking has finite-sample regret upper bounds and a surrogate allocation rule.
literature_map.unoccupied_target: These methods do not control the exact joint randomization tail of a composite weak-order null over compatible deterministic schedules.
literature_map.checked_locations: Jiang et al., Theorems 2--6 and Conclusion; Aronow et al., Lemma 1, Proposition 1, and Section 7; Han et al., Introduction, Theorem 1, and Conclusion.

literature_checklist.author: Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 3.3 transfers simultaneous coverage of pairwise differences into simultaneous rank coverage, including ties through rank intervals.

literature_checklist.author: Rigdon and Hudgens
literature_checklist.one_line: Section 4.1 maximizes randomization \(p\)-values over compatible binary schedules that map to a scalar interference-effect value.

literature_checklist.author: Bazylik, Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 2.1--2.2 give finite-sample rank sets by conditioning multinomial counts to obtain exact binomial pair tests.

literature_checklist.author: Athey, Eckles, and Imbens
literature_checklist.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
literature_checklist.one_line: Proposition 4.1 partitions assignments so a nonsharp interference null is sharp in an artificial conditional experiment.

literature_checklist.author: Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 3.1 and 5.1 give finite-sample saturation tests for individual-level restrictions, while weak average nulls are asymptotic.

literature_checklist.author: Jiang, Imai, and Malani
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 2--5 derive joint covariance and asymptotic tests for multiple saturation mechanisms under two-stage randomization.

literature_checklist.author: Aronow, Green, and Lee
literature_checklist.one_line: Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 give sharp coupling bounds and asymptotically sharp estimation for unidentified randomization variance.

literature_checklist.author: Han, Owusu, and Shin
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 bounds empirical-success ranking regret under clustered interference but does not construct a confidence set.

novelty_justification: {"closest_results":"The two closest published results are Rigdon and Hudgens' scalar exact schedule inversion and Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm's simultaneous rank projection. Bazylik et al. is the closest finite-sample rank result, but its nuisance-removing binomial conditioning relies on multinomial sampling. The July 2026 saturation preprint by Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong is the closest design-specific test paper; it explicitly reserves finite-sample validity for individual-level partially sharp, bounded, or monotone nulls and uses asymptotics for weak averages.","non_subsumption":"Rigdon and Hudgens do not address simultaneous order uncertainty; Mogstad et al. assume an externally valid simultaneous difference region; Bazylik et al. use a multinomial conditional family absent here; Liu et al. test unit-level monotonicity rather than weak average welfare ordering. Han, Owusu, and Shin study ranking risk rather than confidence coverage. No checked paper contains the exact target-method pair.","remaining_risk":"The baseline algorithm is finite but can be exponential in the number of clusters and response types. The publishable field contribution therefore rests on proving the exact table quotient and coverage cleanly; practical pruning and consonant refinement remain open rather than being claimed.","strict_delta":"The new object is a random set of ordered partitions of all quota policies with uniform finite-sample randomization coverage for the complete welfare weak order. Its calibration uses one global schedule-specific max discrepancy and a supremum over compatible binary schedules. The exact response-type/arm/outcome table formula makes this composite inversion finite and removes labeled potential-outcome alignments that cannot affect either welfare or the statistic."}
